matrix.comment: The standing comparison (docs/development/benchmarks.md). Only the frame generation kind is a KSP start of its own; the upscaler, raytracing and Ray Reconstruction (the probe's mod.<key> keys), frame generation on and off and the latency models (the proxy's live keys) are set in turn inside each start. The raytracing's rtBlas*, rtTlasFastTrace and rtMegaGeometry keys go into proxy_load: the meshes are built at the flight's start, before the first phase, so a comparison of them takes a run of its own with other values there; each start's record holds the proxy's lines of its large mesh builds (rt_builds). The radiance cache (the proxy's live rtRadianceCache) is a rendering of its own for one technique and raytracing mode, with the latency models it names; every other phase has it off. So are the opacity micromaps (the proxy's live rtOpacityMicromaps), the last rendering of the start: the first 1 makes the raytracing's pipelines with micromap support, which they keep, and the meshes' structures are rebuilt with them once their micromaps are baked, in the rendering's first seconds; every other phase has it 0. A frame generation kind may write values into the DLSS-G package's ini for its start (dlssg_ini, section by section) and name the renderings it is measured with (only): dlssg-c is the package's preset C ([DLSSG] Preset), with FSR 3 at RT Off and Full and no latency model, as a kind of dlssg for the checks; both DLSS-G starts set [Logging] FrameTiming=1, which writes the GPU time of the frame generation evaluates per frame to the dlssg-logs copied beside the raw logs.
